title: Regeneration and effective correction: completed mechanism evidence

report.text:
# How regeneration can sustain effective correction

Research continuation for Ren, 5 October 2026. This completes the proposed finite mechanism study connecting shared renewal, participant consequences, and materially supported revision of an allocation rule. Earlier theories remain available. The result is a conditional mathematical construction, not an empirical theory of every institution.

**A system can renew its shared productive support while depleting a participant's protected capacity. Under the specified replacement rule, protecting that participant requires a causal route responsive to that harm, and maintaining that route requires funding its repeated use as well as its existence.** The construction below demonstrates both outcomes under the same production technology and initial resources.

This sharpens the proposed connection between generativity and 善. The ethical premise is that an affected participant matters independently of whether the productive system needs that participant to survive. The model explains how one specified protection can be made operational; it does not derive that premise from reproduction or persistence.

## A shared system and an affected participant

The system produces ten resource units per round while its shared productive support satisfies \(E\ge2\); the main comparisons start at \(E=3\). Two units replenish the two units of shared wear. Both allocation rules therefore preserve the shared support stock \(E\). Production presumes continuing access to supplied energy or feedstock; this is not a closed physical universe. The affected participant is a recipient whose protected capacity is not required for this production; this deliberate separation permits testing whether aggregate persistence implies participant protection.

Two supplied rules allocate the remaining output differently. A funding amount \(f\) is reserved for a correction mechanism in either rule:

| Recipient | Restorative rule F | Extractive rule X |
|---|---:|---:|
| Shared productive support | 2 | 2 |
| Correction mechanism | \(f\) | \(f\) |
| Affected participant | 3 | 1 |
| Incumbent operator | \(5-f\) | \(7-f\) |
| Total | 10 | 10 |

The comparison uses nonnegative allocations. At the main threshold \(f=11/9\), both incumbent allocations are positive. X gives the incumbent operator two more units than F. The specified replacement rule installs the higher-current-return rule whenever no effective corrective mandate constrains it. This is a supplied deterministic rule for selection among operating practices, not a complete model of human choice or biological evolution.

The participant has reserve \(B\), capped at six, and needs two units per round to support a specified function. F replenishes one net unit; X removes one. The protected requirement is \(B\ge1\) at the end of every round. At zero, the participant has lost the modeled capacity, including effective access to filing. This is not a claim that the participant literally dies or that this one stock measures their entire well-being.

Under controller-only revision, X keeps being selected. Starting at six, the participant's reserve reaches zero after six rounds, although shared production continues. Thereafter unmet participant needs can accumulate while the aggregate system keeps operating. Monitoring only shared support gives no alarm.

## A correction channel that has to remain usable

The corrective mechanism has its own reserve \(Q\), capacity \(K\), observation channel, and binding allocation gate. It must pay one unit of upkeep at the start of each round. Initiating a claim costs it two additional units, while the participant pays one unit to file. Both bills are due before that round's production arrives. Thus filing requires at least three units already accessible in \(Q\).

If upkeep cannot be paid, the material carrier fails and its gate becomes ineffective. Future allocations do not automatically reconstruct a destroyed carrier. A separate installation mechanism would be needed for that. The stock is a means of operating the specified channel, not a substitute for having the channel or authority in the first place.

The participant protocol files when X is active and \(B\le4\), provided filing is affordable and the corrective carrier operates. Correction has a two-round delay, including the filing round: X remains in effect during those rounds. The gate then installs F until the participant reaches six, when the temporary mandate expires. The incumbent operator's greater private return under X again makes X the selected rule.

This specifies who initiates correction, which observation triggers it, how its costs are paid, what changes the allocation, and when the mandate ends. Automatic filing, the reserved funding stream, and the binding gate are supplied features of this institution. Its strategic acceptance, historical origin, and legitimacy are not inferred from affordability.

## One full round of depletion and restoration

Start with the participant at six and an operational carrier. The exact participant cycle is:

| Round | Effective action | Participant reserve afterward |
|---|---|---:|
| Start | Full participant reserve | 6 |
| 1 | X allocation | 5 |
| 2 | X allocation | 4 |
| 3 | Pay one to file; first delayed X allocation | 2 |
| 4 | Second delayed X allocation | 1 |
| 5 | Binding F allocation | 2 |
| 6 | F allocation | 3 |
| 7 | F allocation | 4 |
| 8 | F allocation | 5 |
| 9 | F allocation; release mandate afterward | 6 |

The restored reserve is the actual starting resource for the next cycle. Over nine rounds, participant receipts total nineteen: four X receipts and five F receipts. Eighteen units support the ordinary function and one pays filing. Nothing is replenished by resetting the state between trials.

The model permits the participant to use the current round's allocation toward that round's ordinary needs. Filing and carrier expenses, in contrast, are prefunded. The end-of-round protection criterion must not be confused with a stricter requirement to prepay every ordinary need while retaining an intraround reserve.

## Exact funding and timing boundaries

Each nine-round cycle requires nine units of carrier upkeep and two units for a claim. With no outside credit or additional subsidy, recurring operation therefore requires

\[
\boxed{f\ge1+\frac29=\frac{11}{9}.}
\]

Below this rate, every successful cycle spends more than it receives. A finite initial reserve can finance only finitely many such cycles. Maintenance-only funding \(f=1\) can keep an idle channel present while failing to finance its continuing use.

The average condition has a separate liquidity requirement:

\[
\boxed{K\ge3.}
\]

Even abundant future funding cannot pay a three-unit prefunded bill through a smaller store. At \(f=11/9\), capacity three and initial carrier reserve three are sufficient. The first two ordinary rounds keep the already full store at three; filing leaves \(11/9\) after current funding arrives; the next eight ordinary rounds restore it to three before the next claim. The resulting cycle can repeat indefinitely. Any initial overflow is recorded rather than reused.

More exactly, at this funding rate the least sufficient initial reserve is \(23/9\) when the participant starts at six, because two ordinary rounds add \(4/9\) before filing. This initialization belongs to the stated phase of the cycle; another initial stage needs its own prefix check.

The participant has a different constraint. If filing occurs at reserve \(h\), filing costs \(c\), and \(d\ge1\) rounds of X follow before restoration, its minimum reserve is \(h-c-d\). Hence

\[
\boxed{h\ge1+c+d.}
\]

For \(h=4,c=1,d=2\), the minimum is exactly one. Waiting one round longer, or adding a third delayed X round, breaches the protection requirement before the favorable rule can act. More money in the carrier cannot replace the participant's missing time or reserve.

These thresholds are sharp for the specified protocol, cost accounting, release rule, and initialization. They do not establish a universal minimum cost of justice or an optimum over all possible institutions. A permanently effective alternative rule could avoid these recurring claims; its implementation would require its own account.

Earlier action also changes recurring cost. Filing at five instead of four keeps the participant's minimum at two, but shortens the cycle to seven rounds. Required recurring funding rises to \(1+2/7=9/7\). The safer timing margin has a specific additional cost under this release rule; an unchanged budget cannot be assumed to pay for it indefinitely.

## What the comparisons establish

An externally fixed F rule is a reference case: it protects the participant without corrective claims, while stipulating that replacement cannot overturn it. It is not evidence that permanent protection is free or naturally maintained.

The meaningful matched comparison holds production, initial stocks, allocated correction funding, and payment rules fixed between controller-only revision and participant-effective revision. The intervention changes which participant signal can activate the binding route. Under the former, the shared system persists while the participant loses capacity. Under the latter, the paid cycle protects both.

The checks separately reduce funding, delay execution, disable effective claim access, and withdraw binding authority. The access switch disables the claim route jointly; it does not isolate sensing from every later stage of communication and execution. A statement of rights, a funded reserve, and a working route to rule change are distinct conditions. The corrected result depends on their conjunction; it is not caused by an undisclosed increase in production.

The exact comparisons include these failures:

| Intervention | Consequence under the specified initial conditions |
|---|---|
| Controller-only revision, same resources | Participant reserve reaches zero in round 6; shared production persists. |
| Carrier funded only for upkeep | One recovery succeeds; participant reserve reaches zero in round 15. |
| A third delayed X round | Participant protection fails in round 5, before restoration takes effect. |
| Funding just below the recurring threshold, with a larger initial reserve | Failure is postponed, not eliminated; the independently checked example fails in round 194. |
| Withdraw funding surplus, effective claim access, or binding authority after the first recovery | Each withdrawal breaks participant protection six rounds later. |

The last interventions locate a remaining dependency: this institution renews correction while its stipulated funding and execution arrangements hold. It does not prove immunity to arbitrary capture of those arrangements. No rescue after a breached floor is counted as uninterrupted protection.

## What this adds to the earlier work

The [retention model](../work/alignment-and-regeneration/model.md) already explains how selection among productive contributors can deplete shared renewal. The other session's [participation analysis](/Users/ren/theories/_process/research/2026-10-04-integrated-evolution/continuing-participation-math.md) already distinguishes consent at different information stages and derives funded-compensation constraints. Its [plural-requirements analysis](/Users/ren/theories/_process/research/2026-10-04-integrated-evolution/plural-correction-math.md) already tests whether one executable policy can meet several requirements together. Those results are inherited here.

The present addition joins recurrent replacement of the allocation rule, participant depletion despite shared persistence, a physically maintained correction channel, delay, and the resources delivered to its next use. It gives an indefinite constructive witness and separate obstructions for recurrent budget, prefunding, and participant timing.

Costly institutional support and selection among governance arrangements have established predecessors. Sigmund and colleagues model paid institutions and second-order free riding; Hilbe and colleagues investigate how institutional choice procedures affect outcomes. Our construction is a local mechanism test within that broader field, with no claim of scientific priority. [Sigmund et al., 2010](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature09203); [Hilbe et al., 2014](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1315273111).

## The connection to generativity and 善

The completed model separates three propositions: the system renews its productive support; the participant retains a protected capacity; and the participant's route to future correction remains usable. The first can hold while the other two fail.

That is the precise limit of judging goodness by the survival of a larger whole. Some affected beings are dispensable to the processes that affect them. Ethical standing asks that their consequences count anyway. Making the declared protection effective in the model requires an explicit protection criterion and a working path through which that criterion can affect outcomes.

Our candidate formulation is therefore:

> **Ethically favorable generativity includes renewing affected beings' worthwhile capacities and their effective means to correct how those capacities are treated.**

This is a proposed ethical commitment joined to a causal mechanism. It does not identify every form of degeneration with moral evil, classify participants by their productivity, or settle all conflicts of welfare, agency, and obligation. The protected stock here measures one capacity, and the supplied protocol supports one kind of complaint.

The bounded plan is completed by the mechanism, comparisons, recurrence proof, and explicit failure boundaries. The broader origin and legitimacy of corrective institutions, unrestricted new threats, and a universal derivation of 善 remain outside what this construction establishes.

## Verification and preservation

The accompanying [evidence record](regeneration-and-effective-correction-evidence.json) retains the full transition rules, exact checks, independent audit, source scopes, and preservation records. Exact enumeration covers all 2,380 canonical states of the specified finite baseline and checks successor closure, resource accounting, and its recurrent states. Of 1,008 states meeting the pointwise protection conditions, 272 preserve them indefinitely under the baseline protocol: present protection alone is insufficient. These counts describe this enumerated state space, not probabilities or universal proportions. A separate implementation checks the cycle and 149 safe parameter cases using exact fractions. The general recurrence and obstruction claims rest on the displayed arguments, not on a long simulation. No biological, clinical, or social experiment is claimed. The new work is additive; earlier theories are not rewritten.

established: An explicit productive arrangement can preserve shared support while depleting a dispensable affected participant.
A supplied funded binding claim protocol can preserve the participant floor through an exactly recurring full-state cycle.
For that protocol, recurring funding, prefunded capacity, phase-specific initialization, and positive-delay timing impose distinct sharp constraints.

reproducible_materials.text:
# A maintained route from participant harm to rule revision

Constructed finite mechanism, 5 October 2026. This note supplies an exact model and proofs for the new investigation. It does not model the invention, legitimacy, or strategic enforcement of the initial protocol. The executable implementation is `check_model.py`; complete results are `model-checks.json`. All Q and ledger entries in the JSON are in ninths of a unit.

## Physical and procedural specification

Shared productive capacity is E, an integer stock with capacity 3. At E≥2, one round yields 10 units, consumes 2 units of shared capacity and replaces those 2 units from its output. Thus E stays constant while production continues. Below 2, production fails and remaining E is consumed. This idealized technology assumes continuing access to an unmodeled feedstock/energy source; it is not a closed physical universe.

An affected participant has a resource reserve B∈{0,…,6}, receives p units of output and has a required draw of 2 per round. The protected floor is B≥1; this is capacity to keep a specified function and communication option available, not a complete welfare measure. A fee of 1 is consumed when a claim is filed. If incoming resources plus reserve cannot cover the draw, the implementation records unmet demand explicitly. B=0 denotes loss of the protected capacity, not biological death. Production does not require this particular participant's activity. Consequently shared production can persist while the participant is deprived.

Two implemented allocation templates have equal gross output and shared renewal:

| Allocation | Shared | Correction carrier | Participant | Incumbent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| F | 2 | f | 3 | 5−f |
| X | 2 | f | 1 | 7−f |

For the principal f=11/9, the incumbent receives 34/9 under F and 52/9 under X. Both cover an incumbent operating requirement of 2 if one is included; the difference of 2 favors X. Outside a binding claim, a supplied current-return comparison/replacement mechanism therefore installs X. This is a stipulated incumbent decision/replacement rule, not a biological selection theorem. Labels F and X name different allocations, not complete judgments about fairness or evil.

The correction carrier has available-work reserve Q∈[0,K]. It must pay upkeep m=1 from existing Q **before** the round's production receipts. A new claim also consumes k=2 from Q before production. If upkeep cannot be paid, the carrier ceases operating, pending or active authority is lost, and subsequent earmarked receipts are discarded rather than magically resurrecting it. A reconstruction procedure is not included. Zero stock immediately after already-paid fees is permissible: that round's service has been paid, and production receipts arrive before the next round's upkeep.

The participant channel has a signal connection and an implemented binding allocation gate. With both available, the following finite protocol operates:

1. Outside an upheld claim, X is selected. If B≤h=4 and the participant can pay 1, filing occurs automatically if Q≥m+k=3. No voluntary bargaining or consent is inferred from this automatic reaction.
2. A filed claim leaves X in force for d=2 rounds, including the filing round. Its processing costs are the initial k plus continuing upkeep. At the end of those rounds, the operative gate imposes F.
3. F remains in force until B reaches its capacity M=6. The claim then releases and current-return replacement again installs X.

The gate, its authority, a correct B signal, allocation templates, thresholds and protected earmark f are supplied parts of the implementation. They are not costless: maintenance and each activation are charged, and access, authority, or earmark withdrawal can disable correction. Their original construction and protection from strategic sabotage are not derived. This is a model of operational reproduction of an already implemented route to correction.

For an operative carrier, with I=1 on filing and 0 otherwise,

\[
Q_{t+1}=\min\{K,Q_t-m-kI_t+f\},
\qquad Q_t\ge m+kI_t.
\]

The inequality is a payment condition, not permission to borrow next round's receipts. Participant accounting is

\[
\tilde B_t=B_t-cI_t,\quad
D_t=\min\{2,\tilde B_t+p_t\},\quad
B_{t+1}=\min\{M,\tilde B_t+p_t-D_t\},\quad c=1.
\]

The implementation tracks the unmet draw 2−D and every cap overflow. Allocation sums to gross output; fees and upkeep are consumed, not returned to the producer. No funding source is counted twice.

## Recurrent correction and exact limits

**Proposition 1: the principal cycle.** Set h=4, d=2, M=6, c=1, K=3, f=11/9. From E∈{2,3}, B=6, Q≥23/9, and an operative carrier with signal and authority, the protocol keeps B≥1 and maintains indefinitely recurrent correction. From Q=23/9 it follows the exact nine-round cycle below. From Q=3, two initial rounds discard excess Q receipts and enter the same cycle.

| Pre-round B | Pre-round Q | Allocation | Filing? | Post-round B | Post-round Q |
|---:|---:|---|---|---:|---:|
| 6 | 23/9 | X | no | 5 | 25/9 |
| 5 | 25/9 | X | no | 4 | 3 |
| 4 | 3 | X | yes | 2 | 11/9 |
| 2 | 11/9 | X | no | 1 | 13/9 |
| 1 | 13/9 | F | no | 2 | 15/9 |
| 2 | 15/9 | F | no | 3 | 17/9 |
| 3 | 17/9 | F | no | 4 | 19/9 |
| 4 | 19/9 | F | no | 5 | 7/3 |
| 5 | 7/3 | F | no | 6 | 23/9 |

**Proof.** Substitute in the payment and participant equations. Every Q prepayment is feasible, the minimum B is 1, the end state equals the initial state, and E is unchanged. Deterministic repetition proves indefinite operation. A finite trajectory alone would not do so; equality of the full state closes the argument. ∎

Cycle accounting independently verifies 90 units of gross output: 18 shared renewal, 11 correction funding, 19 participant allocation, and 42 incumbent allocation. The correction allocation exactly pays 9 units of upkeep and one fee of 2. The participant allocation exactly pays 18 units of draw and one filing fee of 1. Caps discard nothing on this recurrent cycle.

**Proposition 2: sharp thresholds for the supplied protocol.** With M=6, h=4, d=2, c=1 and funded initialization, perpetual protection requires and is possible at:

\[
f\ge\frac{11}{9},\qquad K\ge3.
\]

For f=11/9 and K=3, starting at B=6 in X requires Q₀≥23/9. With generous Q funding and capacity, delay d at threshold h preserves the participant floor precisely when

\[
h-c-d\ge1\qquad(d\ge1).
\]

**Proof of timing.** The participant loses c at filing and one on each of d X rounds, reaching h−c−d before F can replenish it. If this is below 1, the protected condition fails; more money in the correction fund cannot reverse that elapsed loss. If it is at least 1, the subsequent F rounds restore B monotonically.

**Proof of cycle length and funding.** For general M,h,c and d≥1 within this protocol, the X interval before triggering lasts M−h rounds; processing adds d X rounds; restoring the post-processing stock requires M−h+c+d F rounds. Hence

\[
L=2(M-h)+c+2d.
\]

One activation is required in every such cycle. The Q ledger over n cycles, including nonnegative discarded excess W, is

\[
Q_{nL}=Q_0+n\{L(f-m)-k\}-W_{nL}.
\]

If L(f−m)<k, finite Q cannot fund indefinitely many cycles. For the principal parameters L=9, m=1, k=2, giving f≥11/9. At equality, the displayed cycle attains the bound. For any larger f in the admissible budget range, the monotonic Q update funds at least the same actions and clips any surplus. Missing the latest safe trigger cannot restore protection by filing later: a late claim begins at B<4 and its c+d cost crosses the floor. Therefore waiting for funds does not evade the lower bound.

**Proof of liquidity.** A filing requires upfront m+k=3, so K<3 makes it impossible regardless of future income. At K=3 the cycle proves sufficiency. From B=6 the first claim must occur after two ordinary X rounds. These accumulate 2(f−m)=4/9, requiring Q₀+4/9≥3, or Q₀≥23/9. Such Q₀ also pays every earlier upkeep. ∎

These are sharp bounds for this release-at-M protocol. Permanently maintaining F, altering filing rules, adding recovery resources or changing the claim lifetime defines a different model and can change the bounds. For example, a perpetually locked F benchmark has no recurring claim cost.

## Controlled comparisons and failures

All three principal comparisons use the same production, funding f=11/9, capacities, initial stocks and routine correction upkeep:

* **Externally locked F:** B stays 6, E stays 3, and Q stays 3. This is a deliberately external benchmark; it receives permanent protection by stipulation and is not a demonstrated self-maintaining institution.
* **Incumbent-only revision:** participant access is disabled; the current-return rule selects X. At round 6, B=0. Thereafter E=3, Q=3, output remains 10, and one unit of participant draw remains unmet every round. The carrier can remain funded yet fail to translate the participant's condition into binding action. This is not an impossibility result about all possible benevolent controllers.
* **Effective participant channel:** the displayed recurrent correction cycle maintains E, B and the carrier.

At f=m=1 and initial Q=3, one claim can be funded. Q subsequently remains at 1, enough for routine upkeep but insufficient for another activation; B reaches 0 at round 15. A working office and an effective remedy are therefore distinct in this mechanism. A capacity of 26/9 never permits the first filing. Adding one processing round, d=3, crosses the B floor at round 5 even though correction later restores B; eventual recovery does not establish uninterrupted protection.

After the first successful recovery at round 9, the model separately withdraws the protected surplus earmark, participant signal access, and binding authority. All three interventions cause subsequent failure of the participant floor while shared production continues. Thus initial success does not establish that the system can protect its own correction constitution against capture.

## Exact verification and scope

The principal finite state space contains 2,380 canonical states: E=0,…,3, B=0,…,6, Q in ninths from 0 to 3, the ordinary/queued/recovery modes and the absent-carrier state. Every transition was enumerated and all successor states remained inside the space. Every orbit was followed to its exact repeated full state. Of 1,008 initially protected states, 272 remain protected indefinitely. There are seven recurrent attractors; two preserve the protected conditions, one at E=2 and one at E=3.

The code also checks the payment-order threshold, initial liquidity, timing family and intervention comparisons, while auditing resource conservation at every evaluated transition. An independent Fraction implementation by another reviewer reproduces 45 successive principal rounds and examines 149 safe parameter cases independently. The general proof carries the continuum funding claim; the finite sweeps are corroboration rather than proof over every real parameter.

This is an executable conditional mechanism with exact accounting. It establishes neither an empirical institutional law nor that evolution necessarily favors this correction structure. Affected standing, honest information and binding execution are operationalized here, while their origin, legitimacy and strategic robustness remain explicit unsolved parts. The result strengthens the question of regeneration: maintenance of shared production can coexist with deprivation, and preserving correction requires resources, usable access, enforceable consequences and timely operation together.

"""Exact finite accounting for a supplied, maintained participant-recourse protocol.

No external packages; money/usable-work Q is stored in ninths. This is a
constructed finite mechanism, not an empirical or universal ethical model.
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from fractions import Fraction
from itertools import product
from pathlib import Path
import json

SCALE = 9

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class State:
    E: int = 3
    B: int = 6
    Q: int = 27
    mode: str = "X"  # X, F, or D<number of further X rounds>
    carrier: bool = True

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Config:
    capacity: int = 27
    funding: int = 11
    threshold: int = 4
    delay: int = 2
    access: bool = True
    authority: bool = True
    external_fair: bool = False


def advance(s, cfg=Config()):
    """Old stock pays Q upkeep/fee; end-of-round funding cannot pay those fees.

    B pays a filing fee before this round's distribution. A new claim leaves
    X in force for exactly cfg.delay rounds, counting the filing round. An
    operative gate then enforces F until B reaches 6 and releases. Outside
    that constraint the return-comparison mechanism selects X.
    """
    active = s.E >= 2
    upkeep_paid = s.carrier and s.Q >= SCALE
    carrier = upkeep_paid
    q = s.Q - SCALE if carrier else 0
    mode = s.mode if carrier and cfg.authority else "X"
    if cfg.external_fair:
        mode = "F"
    b = s.B
    filed = (active and carrier and cfg.access and cfg.authority and not cfg.external_fair
             and mode == "X" and 1 <= b <= cfg.threshold and q >= 2*SCALE)
    if filed:
        q -= 2*SCALE
        b -= 1
        mode = "F" if cfg.delay == 0 else f"D{cfg.delay}"
    rule = "F" if mode == "F" else "X"
    p = (3 if rule == "F" else 1) if active else 0
    available_b = b + p
    draw = min(2, available_b)
    raw_b = available_b - draw
    overflow_b = max(0, raw_b-6)
    b = min(6, raw_b)
    unmet_b = 2-draw
    if mode.startswith("D"):
        delay = int(mode[1:])
        mode = "F" if delay == 1 else f"D{delay-1}"
    elif mode == "F" and b == 6 and not cfg.external_fair:
        mode = "X"
    income_q = cfg.funding if active else 0
    discarded_q = 0
    if carrier:
        raw_q = q + income_q
        discarded_q = max(0, raw_q-cfg.capacity)
        q = min(cfg.capacity, raw_q)
    else:
        # The carrier cannot spontaneously reappear; unserviceable earmarked
        # receipts are discarded rather than turned into free authority.
        discarded_q = income_q + (s.Q if not upkeep_paid else 0)
        q = 0
    e = s.E if active else 0
    ns = State(e, b, q, mode, carrier)
    gross = 90 if active else 0
    common = 18 if active else 0
    common_wear = 9*(s.E+common//9-e)
    participant = 9*p
    incumbent = gross-common-income_q-participant
    assert min(gross,common,participant,incumbent,income_q)>=0
    assert gross == common+income_q+participant+incumbent
    assert 9*s.E+common == 9*e+common_wear
    # Independently audit participant and Q material accounts, in ninths.
    assert 9*s.B+participant == 9*b+9*draw+9*overflow_b+9*int(filed)
    if carrier:
        assert s.Q+income_q == q+9+18*int(filed)+discarded_q
    else:
        assert s.Q+income_q == discarded_q
    ledger = dict(rule=rule,filed=filed,gross=gross,common=common,common_wear=common_wear,
                  participant=participant,incumbent=incumbent,
                  correction_receipt=income_q,correction_upkeep=9*int(carrier),
                  correction_fee=18*int(filed),participant_fee=9*int(filed),
                  correction_discarded=discarded_q,participant_draw=9*draw,
                  participant_discarded=9*overflow_b,unmet_participant_draw=9*unmet_b,
                  carrier_lost=s.carrier and not carrier)
    return ns, ledger


def safe(s):
    return s.E >= 2 and s.B >= 1 and s.carrier


def orbit(s, cfg=Config()):
    seen = {}
    states=[]
    ledgers=[]
    while s not in seen:
        seen[s]=len(states)
        states.append(s)
        s, ledger = advance(s,cfg)
        ledgers.append(ledger)
    start=seen[s]
    return states,ledgers,start


def packed_orbit(s, cfg=Config()):
    states,ledger,start=orbit(s,cfg)
    bad=[i for i,x in enumerate(states) if not safe(x)]
    cycle_ledger=ledger[start:]
    return dict(initial=asdict(s),config=asdict(cfg),transient_length=start,
                period=len(states)-start,min_B=min(x.B for x in states),

"""Independent exact recurrence check; does not import construction code.

The modeled protocol has a prefunded maintained claim gate, a delayed
protective interval, and compulsory release at the participant reserve cap.
These are supplied transition rules, not strategic-equilibrium claims.
"""

from fractions import Fraction as F
import json
from pathlib import Path


def run(*, ceiling=6, threshold=4, filing_cost=1, delay=2,
        funding=F(11, 9), cap=F(3), initial_q=F(3), rounds=100):
    b, q = F(ceiling), F(initial_q)
    state = 'extract'
    remaining = 0
    rows = []
    for t in range(rounds):
        # An unavailable maintained carrier is a stopping event for this
        # independent check; no post-failure resurrection is assumed.
        if q < 1:
            return rows, 'carrier_unfunded'
        pbill = qbill = 0
        requested = state == 'extract' and b <= threshold
        if requested and q >= 3 and b >= filing_cost:
            pbill, qbill = filing_cost, 2
            state, remaining = 'pending', delay
        mode = 'F' if state == 'protect' else 'X'
        a = 3 if mode == 'F' else 1
        bnext = min(F(ceiling), b - pbill + a - 2)
        qgross = q - 1 - qbill + funding
        qnext = min(cap, qgross)
        row = dict(t=t + 1, b=b, q=q, mode=mode, requested=requested,
                   pbill=pbill, qbill=qbill, bnext=bnext, qnext=qnext,
                   spill=max(F(0), qgross-cap))
        rows.append(row)
        b, q = bnext, qnext
        if b < 1:
            return rows, 'participant_floor'
        if state == 'pending':
            remaining -= 1
            if remaining == 0:
                state = 'protect'
        elif state == 'protect' and b == ceiling:
            state = 'extract'
    return rows, 'horizon'


def main():
    rows, status = run(rounds=45)
    assert status == 'horizon'
    assert [r['bnext'] for r in rows[:9]] == [5, 4, 2, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
    assert [r['mode'] for r in rows[:9]] == ['X'] * 4 + ['F'] * 5
    assert rows[8]['qnext'] == F(23, 9)
    assert min(r['bnext'] for r in rows) == 1
    assert sum(r['qbill'] for r in rows[:9]) == 2
    assert sum(r['pbill'] for r in rows[:9]) == 1
    assert sum(r['spill'] for r in rows[:9]) == F(4, 9)
    # Compare the periodic sections after the initial filling transient.
    canonical = lambda rs: [{k: v for k, v in r.items() if k != 't'} for r in rs]
    assert canonical(rows[9:18]) == canonical(rows[18:27])

    family = 0
    for m in range(3, 11):
        for d in range(1, 4):
            for c in range(1, 3):
                for h in range(c + d + 1, m + 1):
                    length = 2 * (m - h) + c + 2 * d
                    rs, st = run(ceiling=m, threshold=h, filing_cost=c,
                                 delay=d, funding=1+F(2, length), rounds=length * 4)
                    assert st == 'horizon'
                    assert min(r['bnext'] for r in rs) == h - c - d
                    assert [r['t'] for r in rs if r['qbill']] == [m-h+1 + j*length for j in range(4)]
                    assert canonical(rs[length:2*length]) == canonical(rs[2*length:3*length])
                    family += 1

    failures = {}
    for name, args in {
        'less_than_claim_capacity': dict(cap=F(299, 100), initial_q=F(299, 100)),
        'upkeep_only_funding': dict(funding=F(1)),
        'below_recurrent_funding_with_extra_initial_stock': dict(funding=F(11, 9)-F(1, 90), cap=F(5), initial_q=F(5), rounds=500),
        'late_trigger': dict(threshold=3),
        'extra_delay': dict(delay=3),
    }.items():
        rs, st = run(**args)
        assert st != 'horizon', name
        failures[name] = dict(first_failure_round=len(rs), kind=st)

    early, early_status = run(threshold=5, funding=F(9, 7), rounds=28)
    assert early_status == 'horizon'
    assert min(r['bnext'] for r in early) == 2
    assert [r['t'] for r in early if r['qbill']] == [2, 9, 16, 23]

    output = dict(status='all_exact_independent_checks_passed',
                  method='Fraction recurrence independent of author code',
                  generalized_safe_parameter_cases=family,
                  initial_nine_rounds=rows[:9],
                  steady_nine_rounds=rows[9:18],
                  failures=failures,
                  earlier_trigger=dict(threshold=5, minimum_b=2, length=7,
                                       funding_minimum=F(9, 7)),
                  scope='A supplied delayed temporary-gate protocol; no optimality across other protocols.')
    path = Path(__file__).with_name('independent-results.json')
    path.write_text(json.dumps(output, default=str, indent=2) + '\n')
    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in output.items() if k not in ('initial_nine_rounds', 'steady_nine_rounds')}, default=str, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# Independent mechanism audit

Working audit, 5 October 2026. This file states requirements before seeing the new construction, then records independent review of the implemented model. Earlier outputs are preserved. The exercise is a conditional mathematical construction, not a biological or institutional experiment.

## Requirements specified before the new model

The promised advance couples three things: shared renewal, consequences for individual participants, and effective correction of the allocation or governance rule. The last must itself require resources and maintained material carriers. A model that installs an unfailing benevolent controller does not explain the promised coupling.

1. **Independent criteria.** State the shared-support floor, each relevant participant's protected floor, and operational revision access before selecting a policy or judging a run. An aggregate stable equilibrium can violate a participant floor. The criteria are explicit evaluative commitments, not quantities evolution automatically maximizes.
2. **A closed resource account.** Production, shared renewal, private allocations, real maintenance costs, replacement of rule carriers, and interventions belong in one ledger. Internal transfers are not destroyed resources, but inaccessible private reserves cannot silently fund an institutional bill. Prefix affordability matters as well as an average budget.
3. **A physically effective update channel.** A complaint or nominal right must reach a sensor, decision mechanism, and actuator capable of changing the relevant rule. If actual compliance is stipulated, say so; affordability does not create authority. Charge continuing operation and replacement if those are claimed.
4. **Endogenous exposure.** Explain how rule carriers or implementation quality change under incentives, replacement, degradation, or capture. A dynamic rule parameter alone does not derive its execution, historical origin, or legitimacy. An inherited trait with differential return is different from a collectively chosen rule.
5. **Fair comparisons.** Hold production technology, initial endowment, and permitted physical resources fixed across the no-correction, controller-only, and participant-effective variants. State when the action or information sets differ. An extra subsidy or privileged controller cannot be the unreported cause of success.
6. **A viable passage.** A favorable eventual equilibrium is insufficient if protected states fail first. Initial reserves, observation timing, repair delay, and recurring threats must be included. One funded reset is insufficient evidence of indefinite correctability.
7. **Critical ablations.** Test at least one stable shared-stock state with harmful distribution; nominal rights without funded execution; correction with its carrier not replenished; and appropriately matched corrected operation. If a sensor or authority link is claimed essential, removing it must have an explained consequence.
8. **Honest scope.** A prescribed protocol can demonstrate paid, recurring correction. It cannot by itself establish why evolution favors that protocol, how every rule emerged, or that all future threats admit correction. More future activity is not a complete measure of ethical value.

## Prior-art scope within this research program

The prior local `work/alignment-and-regeneration/model.md` already proves that productive contributors with higher retention can spread until shared support collapses, even when replacement stops short of fixation. It explicitly does not model collective authority or correction.

The cross-session file `/Users/ren/theories/_process/research/2026-10-04-integrated-evolution/continuing-participation-math.md` was read in full for this audit. It already distinguishes ex ante agreement from participation after public histories and recommendations, derives positive aggregate surplus with an unaffordable compensation requirement, proves exact one-gate funding cuts, and uses a full-history policy calculation. It also explicitly supplies public observations, committed control, conditional payment, and a permanent passive-refusal option. Merely charging a fee or adding a participation constraint would repeat that work. The useful remaining target is whether the capacity that makes correction effective can persist through recurring degradation and replacement of its own carriers.

## General resource obstruction worth testing

For any construction in which correction load obeys `load' = incoming pressure - completed correction` and a correction reserve obeys `reserve' = funding - upkeep - cost × completed correction`, integration gives a necessary long-run budget condition whenever load stays bounded and reserve stays nonnegative with finite initial endowment. Sustained funding must cover upkeep plus the correction cost of sustained incoming pressure. This is a conservation argument, not a new universal principle. Favorable average balance alone is not sufficient: a delayed bill can exhaust liquidity or a participant's protected reserve before the eventual repair.

Whether that inequality applies depends on the actual model. It must not be imported when correction load is nonlinear, resources can be borrowed, or the relevant threshold has another definition.

## Independent mathematical and implementation review

The construction in `check_model.py` was read directly. I independently implemented the delayed temporary-gate recurrence with exact rational arithmetic in `independent_check.py`, without importing the author's transitions. For 45 main-model rounds, a subsequent direct comparison matched every participant reserve, correction reserve, selected allocation, filing fee, and correction-reserve overflow. The successful end-round participant path is `6 → 5 → 4 → 2 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6`.

The periodic funding calculation is sound for the supplied protocol. A successful nine-round cycle consumes nine correction-upkeep units and two filing units. With finite initial funds and funding below `11/9` per round, infinitely many such cycles are impossible by summing the budget. Every claim has a three-unit prefunded bill, so capacity below three prevents filing even with abundant later receipts. At exact funding, capacity three, and participant initialization six, initial correction reserve `23/9` is both sufficient and necessary for uninterrupted protection. Two initial ordinary rounds raise that stock to three. Starting instead at three discards `4/9` across those initial rounds and then joins the same periodic section. The steady cycle has no correction-reserve overflow.

Protection has a distinct timing condition. For strictly positive integral delay `d`, an integer trigger `h`, and filing cost `c`, with net extraction of one per delayed round, the lowest participant reserve is `h-c-d`. Thus `h >= 1+c+d` is necessary and sufficient for the participant part of this supplied cycle, assuming the claim and ensuing gate are funded. The filing round is included in `d`. For a ceiling `M`, the cycle length is `2(M-h)+c+2d`; this counts pre-claim extraction, delayed extraction, and restoration. The independent checker verified 149 safe parameter combinations, including non-default ceilings and filing costs.

An initial version of the author's parameter sweep included zero delay while using the positive-delay formula. That was a genuine boundary mistake: with immediate restorative allocation, the same-round receipt can replenish a filing debit before the end-round floor is evaluated. The author restricted the theorem and sweep to positive delay; the principal two-round-delay result was unaffected. This correction should remain visible in the audit rather than be described as an unchanged first-pass success.

Additional exact independent failures are recorded in `independent-results.json`. A reserve cap below three fails protection; upkeep-only funding supports one claim but cannot finance ongoing claims; increasing delay or filing too late breaches the participant floor. At funding `11/9 - 1/90`, even initial correction reserve and capacity five merely delay failure until round 194. This separates a recurrent funding obstruction from an inadequate initial endowment.

An earlier trigger illustrates the protocol's resource tradeoff: with `M=6,h=5,c=1,d=2`, the minimum participant reserve rises to two, but the cycle shortens to seven and its necessary recurring funding rises to `9/7`. This is a result within the supplied temporary-mandate rule, not a general price of participant protection.

The author's complete finite-state check considers 2,380 states. Of 1,008 states satisfying the pointwise protected conditions, 272 remain protected indefinitely under the protocol. Thus present safety and eventual attraction must not be substituted for uninterrupted continuation. The finite graph check and the symbolic periodic proof answer complementary questions.

## Final scope and verdict

**Accepted with the corrections and scope statements above.** The main construction provides a resource-balanced, recurring witness in which the same productive technology maintains shared support either with or without participant protection, depending on a funded effective claim route. Exact arithmetic and independent reconstruction support the main cycle, the funding and prefunding cuts, and the positive-delay boundary.

The comparison called controller-only uses the stated private-current-return replacement rule. It is not an impossibility theorem for all controllers: an externally maintained fair rule can protect the participant. In particular, retaining a protective gate permanently or choosing a different correction protocol can change the recurring filing cost. The sharp `11/9` threshold belongs to compulsory release at full reserve followed by renewed extraction.

The model supplies a protected allocation stream, a binding gate, a known participant signal, automatic filing, and the replacement law. Paying maintenance makes their continued operation costly and testable; it does not derive their initial construction, strategic acceptance, legitimacy, or resistance to every kind of capture. A disabled effective-access switch does not independently isolate failures of sensing, decision authority, and actuation, although those are conceptually distinct links. The allocation operator who receives a private residual should be named separately from the material carrier of the corrective channel.

The participant floor is an independently imposed evaluative requirement. Loss of that floor is neither literal death nor a universal measure of well-being. Shared production can continue because this affected participant is not necessary to the modeled production technology. Protecting a dispensable affected participant therefore remains a substantive commitment instead of being smuggled into the definition of aggregate survival.

The previous funding/participation results are inherited, while the new coupling adds repeated rule replacement, continued material operation of a binding route, and the reserve returned to its next use. It is a completed bounded mechanism study, not an explanation of the ultimate emergence of all governance or a derivation of 善 solely from natural selection.

# Sources and ethical scope: maintained correction and participant protection

Audit for Ren's foundational program, 5 October 2026. Existing outputs are preserved. This note distinguishes the proposed construction from preceding work and specifies what its participant result would mean. It is not a claim of scientific originality.

## Prior work already supplies the general machinery

Read `/Users/ren/theories/_process/research/2026-10-04-integrated-evolution/continuing-participation-math.md` and `plural-correction-math.md`.

The participation module already distinguishes agreement before uncertainty from acceptance after a public history or disclosed recommendation. It requires a declared, consequential refusal option; proves the finite stopping-time argument for a committed continuation; accounts for sunk expenditures; derives prefix liquidity and compensation constraints; and gives an exact positive-surplus but unfundable repair example. It explicitly supplies commitment and conditional payment rather than deriving them. The broader theory should reuse these results, not announce them as new.

The plural-correction module already gives a common executable policy satisfying several separately declared requirements, or an inequality excluding every policy in the stipulated class. Its certificates are not welfare weights. It distinguishes expectations from realized protection and explains why aggregate coordinates do not establish individual participation, legitimacy, or fair allocation. The machinery requires declared consequences and bounds.

Earlier source checks also found coupled selection, stock renewal, failed rescue, and costly appropriation rules in `FOUNDATION-ALTERNATIVE-ORIGINAL.md` and `selection-of-renewal.md`. Endogenizing an allocation trait is therefore an extension of this program, not a new explanation of why incentives and resource renewal can conflict.

## Two directly relevant primary predecessors

1. [Sigmund, De Silva, Traulsen, and Hauert (2010), *Social learning promotes institutions for governing the commons*](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature09203). The three-page [author-hosted article](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~hauert/publications/reprints/sigmund_nature10.pdf) was read. Its model compares paid peer and pool punishment, including contributors who do not support sanctioning. Which regime spreads depends on second-order punishment and the permitted participation choices. It does not fully specify implementation of the institution. This is close prior work for costly maintenance of a rule, not a warrant to infer legitimacy from its persistence.

2. [Hilbe, Traulsen, Röhl, and Milinski (2014), *Democratic decisions establish stable authorities that overcome the paradox of second-order punishment*](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1315273111). The five-page [institutional repository article](https://pure.mpg.de/rest/items/item_1909829/component/file_1909830/content) was read. It combines a model with a public-goods experiment comparing repeated choice between institutions with a binding majority choice. Institutional selection and payoffs differed between the treatments. This establishes a specific relevance of governance choice; it is not a general proof that majority rule protects every participant.

No empirical result from either paper was reproduced here. The new construction must be assessed under its own production, reporting, delay, payment, and enforcement assumptions.

## The concrete proposed addition

The mechanism agent proposes two modes with the same productive output and continuing shared reserve. One mode privileges an incumbent while depleting a capacity belonging to another participant, whose capacity is not required for that aggregate production. A participant-report and binding-response channel has its own maintained stock, consumes resources when used, and acts after a delay. The alternative mode restores the participant capacity. Current-return selection can restore the incumbent-favoring mode, making correction a recurring requirement.

The discriminating result is not merely that correction costs something. It is that **aggregate regeneration can coexist with participant depletion, while participant protection requires a separate, recurrently funded causal route**. An alarm triggered only by the shared stock misses the damage by construction. Explicit response delay, participant reserve, and recurrent funding can then be tested together. The particular cycle and thresholds require independent mathematical and executable verification; this source note does not certify them.

This compares two distinct propositions:

- The productive arrangement renews what it needs to continue.
- The arrangement protects the declared capacity of every included participant.

The first does not imply the second when a participant is dispensable to aggregate production. That gap is exactly why moving to a larger system boundary does not, by itself, transform persistence into goodness.

## Concrete evaluation criteria

The finished construction should report separate outcomes, under identical production and initial-resource assumptions:

1. Shared support stays above its declared floor on every modeled step.
2. Each protected participant capacity stays above its own declared floor, including during filing and response delay.
3. The correction mechanism remains capable of its next required operation; its successor capacity and every due payment are actually funded.
4. Participant access is usable at the time harm must be reported. An unaffordable, too-late, or powerless formal permission does not satisfy this operational criterion.

If filing or funding is prescribed by the supplied protocol, say so. If voluntary participation is claimed, compare the participant's consequences under filing and the specified no-filing/refusal option at the actual information history, using the existing participation framework. A physically affordable contribution is not automatically willingly supplied. If the mechanism can reduce the refusal option itself, apparent acceptance requires an additional audit rather than being counted as evidence of freedom.

The binding force of the gate also has to be named as a supplied law or strategy. Materially maintaining a gate can explain when it operates; it does not establish why powerful actors comply, how its authority first appeared, or whether its decisions are legitimate. If strategic compliance is not modeled, describe operational recurrence rather than a self-enforcing institution.

## Ethical interpretation of a successful result

The normative premise is that the protected participant matters independently of whether the productive whole needs that participant. The model makes that premise effective through a specified floor and corrective rule; it does not derive the premise from selection.

A successful test would show how one specified form of participant protection can be renewed alongside material production despite recurrent capture pressure. It would not prove complete welfare, universal justice, or that all participants endorse the regime. Participant capacity is an explicit operational measure, not a synonym for a person's entire good.

For the user's proposed relation between generativity and 善, the advance is consequently precise: ethically favorable generation requires inspecting whose future capacity is renewed, including people whose deprivation would not interrupt the system. The system's ability to correct such deprivation is itself a capacity that must be kept alive. This yields a concrete investigation of good generativity without declaring that every persistent or expanding organization is good.

# Final source and ethical-scope review

Reviewed `outputs/regeneration-and-effective-correction.md` as available on 5 October 2026, before the evidence package was created. This review concerns claims, sources, and completion scope; the independent mathematical audit and exact transition checks carry verification of the recurrence and thresholds.

## Verdict

The report has no material ethical or source-scope blocker. Its bounded completion claim is warranted once the cited evidence package and independent verification are finalized. The requested study supplies a causal mechanism, matched comparisons, an indefinitely recurrent protection witness, and separate obstructions. It does not need to solve the origin of authority or universal morality to complete this declared construction.

The draft explicitly identifies automatic filing, reserved funding, binding authority, and the replacement rule as supplied protocol features. It does not conflate affordability with voluntary participation or strategic compliance. 1. Opening: replace “Protecting that participant requires a separate causal route” with “Under the specified replacement rule, protecting that participant requires a causal route responsive to that harm.” The unrestricted original could be read as a universal necessity; the report's own externally fixed restorative rule makes clear that the necessity is conditional on the mechanism being tested.

Ethical interpretation: replace “Giving them standing in the model requires an explicit protection criterion and a working path through which that criterion can affect outcomes” with “Making the declared protection effective in the model requires an explicit protection criterion and a working path through which that criterion can affect outcomes.” Moral standing need not disappear when protection is unenforceable. The construction explains effectiveness of one supplied protection rather than creation of the participant's value.

Neither edit changes the mechanism or requires rerunning numerical checks. These are scope refinements, not requests for another research phase.

The defensible finished claim is that a specified material channel can repeatedly protect a participant whom aggregate production could otherwise disregard, provided its operation, timely use, and next use are funded. The report correctly leaves strategic acceptance, legitimacy, additional threats, and a universal derivation of 善 outside that result. Those exclusions do not make the bounded study incomplete.
